sentences.text: This appeal by the claimants under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 22.11.2019 passed by IInd M.A.C.T, Jaora, district Ratlam in Claim Case No.30/2017 seeking compensation for the death of Ghulam Hussain in the motor accident.

2. Short facts relevant and necessary for the disposal of this appeal are that on 10.02.2017 the deceased Ghulam Hussain was working as labourer and putting sand on the path which was muddy so that vehicle can pass through the muddy road at Manyakhedi River Road, Police Station Ringnod,
district Ratlam.
While doing so tractor bearing registration no.MP-43-AB-4404 which was being driven by respondent No.2 rashly and negligently dashed the deceased and the tractor ran over him.
He was taken to hospital and declared brought dead.

The inquest was made on the very same day and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23300 2 MA-7103-2019 statement of witnesses were recorded wherein it has been deposed that tractor owned by one Habib Khan s/o Akhtar Khan had caused the accident.

The tribunal after trial assessed the compensation of Rs.12,79,600/- for the death of Ghulam Hussain, however, held that the claimants are not entitled for receiving the said compensation on the ground that the claimants failed to prove that the accident was caused by the offending vehicle in question.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant/owner of the offending vehicle taking exception to the impugned award pointed out that although at the time of accident the offending vehicle was having Shabbo Bee vs Jagdish on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126530408/
1 a valid and effective permit but he could not produce the same before the Tribunal as he remained ex-parte before the Tribunal.

sentences.text: Therefore, the Tribunal has committed an error in holding that at the time of accident the offending vehicle was not having any valid permit which is a breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy and directed the insurance company to pay the compensation amount and recover the same from the owner and driver.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent no.3/Insurance company has supported the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.
5.

During the pendency of this appeal, appellants have also filed an application under Order 41 Rule 27 CPC (IA No.4453/2024) seeking to take on record certain documents i.e. copy of the final report,
copy of seizure memo and copy of the agreement dated 15.12.2015 and I.A.No.7482/2024, an application under Order 1 Rule 10 CPC for impleadment of Habib Kha as respondent.

The police had r e c o v e r e d t h e s a i d a g r e e m e n t e x e c u t e d b e t w e e n N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2024:MPHC-IND:23300 3 MA-7103-2019 the respondent no.2 and Habib Khan from the possession of respondent no.2.

This document had also formed a part of the charge sheet which reflects that respondent no.2 had sold the offending vehicle to Habib Khan on 15.12.2015 and the respondent no.1 had also sworn in an affidavit in support of the transaction and had signed form no.29 and 30 of the Motor Vehicles Rules for the use of RTO in respect of transferring the name of said Habib Khan.
He further submits that these documents are essential for the proper adjudication of this appeal and they could not have been placed on record due to inadvertence.

He further submits that the tribunal has dismissed the claim on the ground that appellant no.1 in her statement had disclosed the name of the respondent no.2 as owner of the offending vehicle whereas the charge sheet reflected one Habib Kha as the owner of the offending vehicle.

Therefore, prays for taking it on record as additional evidence and also prayed for remanding back the matter to the Claims Tribunal for deciding the matter afresh on the basis of the additional evidence which have been filed by the appellants.
6.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company opposes the application and prayed for its rejection.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

8. Order 41 Rule 27 of the CPC reads as under:
27. Production of additional evidence in Appellate Court.--(1) The parties to an appeal shall not be entitled to produce additional evidence, whether oral or documentary, in the Appellate Court.

But if -- (a) the Court from whose decree the appeal is preferred has refused to admit evidence which ought to have been admitted, or (aa) the party seeking to produce additional evidence, establishes that NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23300 4 MA-7103-2019 notwithstanding the exercise of due diligence, such evidence was not within his knowledge or could not, after the exercise of due diligence, be produced by Shabbo Bee vs Jagdish on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126530408/
2 him at the time when the decree appealed against was passed,

or]
(b) the Appellate Court requires any document to be produced or any witness to be examined to enable it to pronounce judgment, or for any other substantial cause, the Appellate Court may allow such evidence or document to be produced, or witness to be examined.
(2) Wherever additional evidence is allowed to be produced by an Appellate Court, the Court shall record the reason for its admission.

9. Perusal of the aforesaid provision makes it clear that the appellate Court may allow such evidence to be taken as additional evidence if the documents are necessary for proper adjudication of the case.
In the considered opinion of this Court, the said documents are essential documents for the proper adjudication of the claim petition filed by the legal representatives of the deceased Gulam Hussain.

10. Accordingly, considering the above provision of law, in the considered opinion of this Court, the documents produced by the appellant are essential documents for adjudication of the claim petition filed by the claimants.
Accordingly, IA No.4453/24 & I.A.No.7482/24 are allowed and the documents which are filed by the appellant are taken on record and Habib Kha is permitted to be impleaded as respondent.

The finding recorded by the tribunal to the extent that "the accident which was caused by the offending vehicle in question is not proved, therefore, the claimants are not entitled for compensation and the claim petition is dismissed" is hereby set aside and the matter is remanded back to the Claims Tribunal along with the documents which are filed along with the application under Order 41 Rule 27 CPC and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23300 5 MA-7103-2019 Order 1 Rule 10 CPC which are taken on record along with the record of the Tribunal for deciding the matter afresh on the question of entitlement of compensation by the claimants afresh in the light of the additional evidence which is taken on record.
Needless to say that opportunity of hearing shall also be given to both parties before deciding the said issue afresh.
11. In view of above, the appeal stands disposed of.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE hk/
